articles.title: 29-year-old tennis player, hailing from Novak Djokovic's country, handed 24-year ban
articles.summary: Stefan Milicevic has been banned from the sport until October 2050 after being charged with match-fixing and attempting to recruit players into an alleged
articles.body: Stefan Milicevic has been banned from the sport until October 2050 after being charged with match-fixing and attempting to recruit players into an alleged corruption network. The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) announced the suspension on Thursday, along with a $70,000 fine.Milicevic hails from Serbia, a country with a rich tennis tradition that has produced several world-class players, most notably Novak Djokovic.The 29-year-old was accused of fixing six matches, five of which he played in, and attempting to manipulate the outcomes of six additional matches between 2022 and 2024.The ITIA also charged him with recruiting or trying to recruit several professional players into a network allegedly involved in match-fixing during that period.Milicevic, who mainly competed in lower-tier tournaments, achieved a career-best singles ranking of 1,338 in 2014. According to the ITIA, the alleged network led to other players fixing matches. However, the agency did not reveal the specific matches involved or name the other players suspected of taking part.The ITIA said Milicevic failed to cooperate with its investigation and did not respond to its findings, despite seven attempts to contact him. His lack of engagement was cited as a factor in determining the severity of the sanction.Under the terms of the ban, Milicevic is prohibited from competing in, coaching at or attending tournaments organised or sanctioned by the ATP, WTA, Grand Slams, World Tennis or any national tennis association.The suspension will keep him out of the sport until he turns 53.Folliot also banned for 20 yearsMilicevic's punishment comes after French tennis player Quentin Folliot received a 20-year ban in December following an investigation that identified him as a central figure in an alleged match-fixing network operating on behalf of a syndicate.Folliot, who reached a career-high singles ranking of 488 in 2022, denied allegations concerning 11 matches played between 2022 and 2024. articles.title: Wuhan Open: Britain's Sonay Kartal beats Elina Svitolina to reach semi-finals
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal's winning streak following a long injury lay-off continues as she seals a hard-fought victory over fifth seed Elina Svitolina in the quarter-finals of the Wuhan Open.
articles.body:
Sonay Kartal had a difficult decision to make when she felt ready to rejoin the WTA Tour, having not played for six months because of a debilitating back injury.

Did the 24-year-old Briton ease herself in more gently at lower-ranked tournaments?

Or did the former world number 54 use a protected injury ranking to enter WTA 1000 events in China, where the world's best players compete at the pinnacle of the women's tour?

Kartal chose the latter option - and it is paying off handsomely.

On Friday, she beat world number six Elina Svitolina at the Wuhan Open to reach the first WTA 1000 semi-final of her career.

"I didn't expect to be back at this level this quickly – I don't think many people did," Kartal said.

"I knew it would be a tough choice. I didn't know how I was going to be on the match court – it's very easy to train well but the match scenario is completely different.

"I decided to throw myself in the deep end and play the best players in the world.

"It's worked out good so far. The risk has paid off."

Serb player banned to 2050 for tennis match-fixing

Patience has been paramount for Kartal, who announced herself to the wider British public by reaching the fourth round at Wimbledon last year, as she dealt with a stress fracture in her back.

Kartal had earned impressive victories over 2025 Australian Open champion Madison Keys and 2024 US Open semi-finalist Emma Navarro at Indian Wells in March, but was forced to retire from a fourth-round meeting with now world number one Elena Rybakina.

The issue proved more serious than first thought, leading to the longest absence from competitive action of Kartal's career.

But she has returned to the WTA Tour playing like she has never been away.

Known for her consistent hitting from the baseline, supreme athleticism and tenacity, Kartal added Ukraine's Svitolina to her list of high-profile victories in Wuhan with a 6-2 2-6 6-4 triumph.

Kartal beat Italian 15th seed Jasmine Paolini - a Wimbledon and French Open finalist in 2024 - in the last 16, backing up the win over Swiss ninth seed Belinda Bencic - who won the Tokyo Olympic title in 2021 - in the second round.

Since returning to competitive action little more than three weeks ago - when she represented Great Britain at the BJK Cup - Kartal has won six of her eight matches.

Next up is 2017 French Open champion Jeļena Ostapenko, who came through a tense opening set to beat 11th seed Diana Shnaider 7-6 (8-6) 6-1.

Kartal is only the second British player, after Johanna Konta, to reach a WTA 1000 semi-final since the format's introduction in 2009.

"It's one of the best tennis weeks of my life - results-wise you could say it is the best," Kartal said.

"I'm very happy to be back at this level. It's easy to come out and play a blinder in one match, but I'm happy I have kept this consistency."

How Kartal claimed another notable scalp

Kartal had not dropped a set during her run to the Wuhan quarter-finals, and she broke Svitolina early in the first to start on a positive note.

Svitolina then called for a medical timeout for treatment on her right arm, but she came back strong to take the contest to a decider.

The two players were evenly matched in the third set but it was Kartal who managed to break Svitolina's serve at 5-4 and book her place in the last four.

Speaking on court after her victory, Kartal said she knew "what a great fighter" Svitolina is, so she "was never safe" in the match.

"It was solid composure from me throughout," she added.

"I love playing here and on this court. The atmosphere was amazing, so big thank you to the crowd."

In the other quarter-finals, Polish 16th seed Maja Chwalinska beat Greek Maria Sakkari, while American Ann Li takes on six-time Grand Slam winner and seventh seed Iga Swiatek.

articles.title: Sonay Kartal: Brit breaks new ground by upsetting Elina Svitolina to reach Wuhan Open semi-finals
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal will play Jelena Ostapenko in last four of WTA 1000 event in China from 10am Saturday; watch WTA Wuhan Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Kartal continued her incredible form by defeating fifth seed Elina Svitolina 6-2 2-6 6-4.

She will take on former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko on Saturday for a spot in Sunday's final.

Speaking on-court, Kartal said: "Despite winning the first set pretty comfortably, I knew what a great fighter she [Svitolina] is, so I knew that until the very last point was played, I was never safe.

"Super proud of the determination I managed to show in that match, and I just think it was solid composure from me throughout."

She added: "I'm breaking new ground this week. I've never reached a semis of a WTA 1000 and like I've said I absolutely love playing here and playing on these courts. The atmosphere was amazing today."

After reaching the fourth round of Indian Wells in March, Kartal, 24, missed six months with a stress fracture in her back, returning last month at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals.

Kartal, previously ranked as high as No 44 in the world, reached the third round in Beijing last week.

In Wuhan, she has swept past world No 48 Anhelina Kalinina, world No 12 Belinda Bencic, two-time Grand Slam singles finalist Jasmine Paolini, and now four-time major semi-finalist Svitolina.

Currently 170th in the WTA rankings, Kartal will break back into the top 100 - she is at No 87 following her latest win - after becoming the lowest-ranked player to reach the semi-finals in Wuhan.

She missed three of this year's four Grand Slams, including Wimbledon.

Ostapenko came from 5-2 down in the first set to defeat 11tth seed Diana Shnaider 7-6 (8-6) 6-1.

The Latvian's 32 winners in the match took her tally to 138 for the week.

Who would want to play Kartal right now?

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis , pundit Naomi Broady said: "I don't think Ostapenko is going to enjoy Kartal's game style with the amount of balls Sonay is going to put back into play.

"It will be interesting because when Svitolina upped her aggression in that match, Sonay wasn't all that comfortable in set two, but, of course, it's Ostapenko's base game, isn't it?

"But Sonay is going to be expecting that. She's seeing the ball big, so it's going to be all about keeping the ball out of the strike zone.

"Ostapenko has withdrawn from the doubles here - possibly struggling with the forearm injury - because we saw the physio coming out a couple of rounds ago against Jessica Pegula and she has had it taped since.

"She is not going to enjoy having someone like Kartal down the other end of the court. I think when the pressure is on Ostapenko's back she doesn't always perform her best."

American Ann Li, who upset top seed Aryna Sabalenka in the second round, was unable to cause another shock with Iga Swiatek triumphing 6-4 6-1.

She will play Maja Chwalinska in an all-Polish derby after the French Open finalist came out on top against a resurgent Maria Sakkari 6-0 3-6 7-5.

Spanish wonderkid to face Medvedev for spot in Shanghai final

Rafael Jodar became the youngest semi-finalist in Shanghai Masters history after advancing with victory against Casper Ruud.

The 20-year-old Spaniard was a set down and rallied to a 4-6 6-4 6-3 win.

It was the fourth straight match at the ATP Masters 1000 event that Jodar had mounted a comeback from losing the first set.

He will face Daniil Medvedev for a place in the final after the former US Open champion beat Tommy Paul 6-3 1-6 6-3.

articles.title: A qué hora es el Davidovich - Zverev: horario y dónde ver las semifinales del Masters 1000 de Shanghái
articles.standfirst: El alemán domina los enfrentamientos entre ambos por seis victorias a una
articles.summary: El alemán domina los enfrentamientos entre ambos por seis victorias a una
articles.body: Alejandro Davidovich buscará este sábado la final del Masters 1000 de Shanghái contra el tenista más en forma del momento y que no es otro que Alexander Zverev. El alemán, doble campeón de Grand Slam y que terminará la temporada de número 1 ATP, está en el mejor momento de su carrera a los 29 años. Sascha se ha impuesto en seis de los siete precedentes con el malagueño. La semifinal entre Alexander Zverev (1) y Alejandro Davidovich (25) se disputará en la pista central del Qi Zhong de Shanghái, a las 10:30 horas en España. La segunda semifinal, con la presencia de Rafa Jódar, no se iniciará antes de las 13.00 horas. El duelo de la penúltima ronda del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, entre Alexander Zverev y Alejandro Davidovich, se podrá seguir por Movistar plus. articles.title: Jódar pide perdón al recogepelotas: "Fue un error, no debería haberle tratado así, estaba frustrado"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño se disculpa tras el 'warning' recibido el miércoles en los octavos por abuso verbal
articles.summary: El madrileño se disculpa tras el 'warning' recibido el miércoles en los octavos por abuso verbal
articles.body: Rafa Jódar, al que el pasado miércoles le señalizaron una amonestación verbal por dirigirse a un recogepelotas con estas palabras "dame la p... toalla", ha pedido perdón por sus palabras. "Fue un error. Después del partido estuve reflexionando y me di cuenta de que no debería haber tratado así al recogepelotas. Estaba frustrado por cómo iba el partido para mí. No soy perfecto, soy humano y cometo errores. Así que aprenderé de este error para no repetirlo. Así como estoy aprendiendo cómo hacer el revés o cómo hacer la derecha o cómo hacer el saque, también estoy aprendiendo cómo comportarme en la pista". Jódar, que se ha clasificado este viernes para las semifinales del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, pasa página y comenta que "intentaré no volver a hacerlo porque esa no es la forma correcta de tratar a los recogepelotas, y respeto mucho su trabajo". Rafa pretende disculparse en persona si vuelve a coincidir con el recogepelotas: "Me gustaría, sí, disculparme con el recogepelotas. Si tengo alguna oportunidad de verlo aquí en el recinto, intentaré decirle que lo siento mucho por mi comportamiento y la forma en que actué en ese momento, y nunca volveré a hacerlo".

images.caption: Jódar, en un momento del partido.

articles.title: Badosa habla acerca de su separación profesional con su ex entrenador: "Yo tomé la decisión"
articles.standfirst: La española rompe su silencio y afirma que fue ella quién tomó la decisión de romper la relación profesional con Pol Toledo
articles.summary: La española rompe su silencio y afirma que fue ella quién tomó la decisión de romper la relación profesional con Pol Toledo
articles.body: Paula Badosa y su ex entrenador, Pol Toledo, decidieron poner fin a su relación profesional hace tan solo dos días. Este viernes, la tenista de Begur, ha roto su silencio y ha compartido un breve mensaje en sus redes sociales. "Tras los informes recientes, quiero aclarar que yo tomé la decisión de finalizar mi camino profesional con Pol. Estoy agradecida por nuestro tiempo juntos y le deseo todo lo mejor", así ha confirmado Paula que la decisión de finalizar el vínculo jugadora-entrenador ha sido suya. También ha querido aclarar que, para lo que resta de temporada, no habrá remplazo: "Por lo que queda de la temporada, seguiré trabajando con mi equipo actual, enfocándome en mi tenis y disfrutando de la competición. Con ganas de terminar el año con fuerza y emocionada por lo que viene en 2027", cerró la española.

articles.title: A qué hora es el Jódar - Medvedev: horario y dónde ver las semifinales del Masters 1000 de Shanghái
articles.standfirst: Será el primer enfrentamiento entre el madrileño y el ruso en el circuito ATP
articles.summary: Será el primer enfrentamiento entre el madrileño y el ruso en el circuito ATP
articles.body: Rafa Jódar pondrá a prueba la racha de Daniil Medvedev en China en las semifinales del Masters 1000 de Shanghái. El ruso, campeón de Hangzhou y semifinalista en Pekín, donde fue descalificado ante Novak Djokovic, se medirá al joven madrileño este sábado por un puesto en la final. Medvedev, quinto cabeza de serie, necesitó de tres sets para deshacerse en los cuartos del estadounidense Tommy Paul, por 6-3, 1-6 y 6-3. No hay precedentes en el circuito entre Jódar y el moscovita. Este es el único campeón del torneo que resta en competición. Se impuso en la edición de 2019. El partido entre Rafa Jódar (12) y Daniil Medvedev (5) será la segunda semifinal del Masters 1000 de Shanghái. El duelo está programado no antes de las 13:00 horas en España. La semifinal del Masters 1000 de Shanghái entre Rafa Jódar y Daniil Medvedev se podrá seguir a través de Movistar Plus. Además de poder seguir toda la actualidad a través de MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Swiatek, la única top10 superviviente en las semifinales de Wuhan
articles.standfirst: Elina Svitolina, la otra top10 restante en cuartos, ha cedido en tres sets
articles.summary: Elina Svitolina, la otra top10 restante en cuartos, ha cedido en tres sets
articles.body: Iga Swiatek va directa a por el título en Wuhan. Tras la derrota de la sexta raqueta del mundo, Elina Svitolina, la tenista polaca es la única miembro del top10 del ranking femenino en clasificarse a las semifinales del WTA 1000 asiático. Ha derrotado a la americana Ann Li, verdugo de Aryna Sabalenka, por 6-4 y 6-1 para alcanzar su cuarta semifinal en torneos de categoría 1000 esta temporada. Esta victoria le ha permitido mejorar el resultado que obtuvo en 2025 cuando cedió ante la italiana Jasmine Paolini en cuartos de final. Y es la única tenista en activo en alcanzar todas las semifinales de los 10 WTA 1000 que componen el circuito femenino. Iga sabe que se está jugando estar en las WTA Finals de Indian Wells (7-14 de noviembre) y su desempeño en la ciudad china de Wuhan será clave para ello. Actualmente cuenta con 3.999 puntos en su haber, a 774 de la checa Karolina Muchova (4.773), que marca la séptima posición del ranking y la que cierra la clasificación al torneo de las ocho mejores del año. Linda Noskova, octava del mundo, ya tiene asegurada su plaza por ser campeona de Grand Slam en 2026. Tras Wuhan, el siguiente torneo que tiene la polaca en su agenda es el WTA 500 de Tokio (26 de octubre-1 de noviembre). Donde no participó en la edición del año pasado, otra oportunidad para sumar puntos. Sin embargo, Muchova defiende los cuartos de final. Aryna Sabalenka, Mirra Andreeva, Jessica Pegula, la mencionada Elina Svitolina, Karolina Muchova y Marta Kostyuk, las otras top10 que participaron en el certamen, han caído eliminadas. La número 1, Elena Rybakina, Coco Gauff y Linda Noskova no lo han disputado. Iga Swiatek es la única superviviente de la masacre de Wuhan, y quiere aprovecharlo. Se las verá con su compatriota y flamante finalista de Roland Garros, Maja Chwalinska (22) en la segunda semifinal de mañana.

Swiatek pega de revés. EFE

articles.title: Medvedev pone en juego su racha por China ante Jódar en semifinales
articles.standfirst: El ruso supera a Paul en tres sets y ha ganado 11 de los 12 partidos de la gira
articles.summary: El ruso supera a Paul en tres sets y ha ganado 11 de los 12 partidos de la gira
articles.body: Daniil Medvedev, quinto cabeza de serie del cuadro y campeón de Shanghái en 2019, se las verá este sábado con Rafa Jódar por un puesto en la final. El ruso se ganó el billete tras derrotar en cuartos al estadounidense Tommy Paul, por 6-3, 1-6 y 6-3. Medvedev es el mejor tenista de la temporada sobre superficie dura donde colecciona 34 victorias, una más que Alexander Zverev. Medvedev ha decantado a su favor 11 de los 12 partidos disputados en su particular gira por China. Campeón de Hangzhou y semifinalista de Pekín, repite entre los cuatro mejores en el TMS de Shanghái. La superficie rápida de la central del Qi Zhong le viene como anillo al dedo al moscovita. A sus 30 años, alcanza su 70º semifinal, 19 de las cuales son en torneos de categoría Masters 1000. Iguala en esta estadística a Lleyton Hewitt y Tomas Berdych, pero aún está lejos del récord de 80 en posesión de Novak Djokovic. Daniil es sexto de la Race 2026 y uno de los tenistas, junto a Jódar, que opta a las cinco plazas restantes para las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre).

articles.title: Sonay Kartal: British star says she is due a couple of new tattoos after reaching Wuhan Open semi-finals
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal is enjoying incredible run in China following injury-ravaged season; British player takes on Jelena Ostapenko on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Tennis from 10am; Kartal says she is enjoying "one of the best weeks" of her life
articles.body:
Kartal claimed one of the biggest wins of the career as she beat world No 6 Elina Svitolina on Friday .

The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, seized her first match-point opportunity to complete another stunning victory.

Kartal, who made her breakthrough by reaching the fourth round of last year's Wimbledon, advanced to the last four of a WTA 1000 event for the first time.

"Definitely one of the best weeks of my life," she said. "You could say, results-wise, that is definitely the best for me so far.

"I'm very happy to be backing up the level each day. I think it's pretty easy for a player to come out and play a blinder for just one match. I'm very happy that I managed to keep the consistency. I've got some of my best wins this week."

Kartal added she is due a couple of new tattoos. She had one booked in but was forced to make a last-minute cancellation after heading to the Billie Jean King Cup with Great Britain.

Asked if she would get one done if she won in Wuhan, the Brighton-based star replied with a smile: "I would have to have a think. I can't make a rush decision."

Kartal, using a protected injury ranking to play, has previously peaked at No 44 in the rankings and started the Wuhan Open at No 170, but she has skyrocketed 83 places to No 87 in the live rankings with her run to the semi-finals.

She is assured of adding 390 points to her total, meaning she is guaranteed to be the new British No 2 behind Katie Boulter (No 58), moving past Fran Jones (No 98) and Emma Raducanu (No 109).

Having missed more than six months, Kartal admitted she would not be able to walk without some form of pain but found it "pretty smooth sailing" after a couple of months.

And now she is feeling fit and healthy again.

"My back is great," Kartal said. "I wouldn't have made the return if it wasn't great.

"I think the body is feeling it having not played a tennis match for six months, and when you're on tour, your body gets used to the aches and pains and demands of matches each week. I'm definitely more sore in areas.

"I think if there's one thing I've learned in the six months - it's sometimes patience is the better option. And the heroic thing to do is not play every single week. I feel great and I'm ready to get going for the remainder of the year."

She'll next face Latvian world No 34 Jelena Ostapenko , who beat Diana Shnaider in her quarter-final.

The pair have met twice before, with both matches coming on grass in the space of six days in June 2025 - Ostapenko won at Eastbourne, but then Kartal came out on top at Wimbledon.

"I've enjoyed playing her," said Kartal. "I think we're equal on the scoreboard. But I think there's a level of respect that she shows me.

"She's playing great this week having had a few tough matches, so she's definitely on form. I'm excited for another battle.

"I feel it's going to be a completely different game style to the people that I've played the past few days. I'm ready for a long one if it's needed."

articles.title: Las finales del circuito mundial de tenis en silla de ruedas se jugarán del 9 al 15 de noviembre en Cornellà
articles.standfirst: Los españoles Martín de la Puente y Daniel Caverzaschi, entre los favoritos
articles.summary: Los españoles Martín de la Puente y Daniel Caverzaschi, entre los favoritos
articles.body: World Tennis ha anunciado una nueva denominación para los torneos que ponen fin a la temporada mundial del tenis en silla de ruedas: el Wheelchair Tennis Masters se dividirá a partir de ahora en dos competiciones, las NEC Wheelchair Singles Finals, para individuales, y las UNIQLO Wheelchair Doubles Finals, para dobles. Barcelona acogerá la primera edición de ambas competiciones bajo esta nueva denominación del 9 al 15 de noviembre de 2026, tras la aprobación del cambio en la Asamblea General Anual de World Tennis, celebrada en Almaty (Kazajistán). Ambas competiciones reunirán a los mejores del mundo de la especialidad, incluidas las categorías masculina, femenina y quad, para disputar los últimos títulos de la temporada del UNIQLO Wheelchair Tennis Tour. Las finales se celebrarán en el Centre Internacional de Tennis de Cornellà, que acogerá por primera vez una competición internacional de tenis en silla de ruedas. La cita regresará a Barcelona por segunda vez en cuatro años, después de que la ciudad acogiera en 2023 las finales individuales y de dobles del Masters. Organizado por la Federación Catalana de Tenis, el evento contará con algunas de las principales figuras internacionales de la modalidad, entre ellas Tokito Oda (Japón), Alfie Hewett (Gran Bretaña), Gustavo Fernandez (Argentina) Yui Kamiji (Japón), Diede de Groot (Países Bajos), Niels Vink (Países Bajos) y Sam Schröder (Países Bajos).

articles.title: The future of the Wuhan Open is called into question after big names withdraw from 2026 tournament
articles.summary: The 2026 Wuhan Open suffered several big-name withdrawals. World number one Elena Rybakina withdrew from the Wuhan Open after losing early in Beijing, but sh...
articles.body:
The 2026 Wuhan Open suffered several big-name withdrawals.

World number one Elena Rybakina withdrew from the Wuhan Open after losing early in Beijing, but she wasn't the only top-10 player to drop out of the year's final WTA 1000 event.

After the China Open final, Mirra Andreeva and Qinwen Zheng both chose to skip Wuhan . The Russian cited a schedule change for her withdrawal, while Zheng argued she had injured her shoulder during her victory on home soil.

Former world number one and Andreeva's countryman, Yevgeny Kafelnikov , has now delivered his verdict on her and others withdrawing from the Wuhan Open, suggesting what it could mean for the future of the event.

Yevgeny Kafelnikov believes Wuhan Open withdrawals affect 'the potential hosting of the tournament in the future'

"There are surely some reasons [why Zheng and Andreeva withdrew], because, objectively, she doesn't need to [play] right now. She has already qualified for the WTA Finals in America. She doesn't need to earn any additional points. If she had been seventh or eighth, I am sure she would have played. But right now, this tournament doesn't mean anything to her," said Kafelnikov during the latest episode of ' Hardcourt ' (translated from Russian).

"Of course, it's a real shame, because as I've said so many times, sponsors need to be supported, and with the withdrawals of such leading players in women's tennis, it really affects the potential hosting of the tournament in the future. So the fact that Elena [Rybakina], Mirra [Andreeva], and the others withdrew is, of course, not great."

Kafelnikov is concerned that the Wuhan Open may struggle to attract sponsors in the future after so many of the biggest draws chose to skip this year's event. Without sponsors, the event will likely lose its place on the WTA calendar.

A lot has been made of the Wuhan Open withdrawals, but just how bad has it been? Rybakina and Coco Gauff were two of the first to announce their withdrawals and were soon followed by another 10 players, including Andreeva, Zheng, and Naomi Osaka.

Elena Rybakina (WTA #1) – Left foot injury

Victoria Mboko (WTA #15) – Left knee injury

Amanda Anisimova (WTA #17) – Wrist injury

Mirra Andreeva (WTA #3) – Schedule change

Linda Noskova (WTA #8) – Left calf injury

Naomi Osaka (WTA #18) – Physical strains

Qinwen Zheng (WTA #23) – Shoulder injury

Anastasia Potapova (WTA #26) – Right shoulder injury

Barbora Krejcikova (WTA #46) – Back injury

Oleksandra Oliynykova – (WTA #51) – Ankle injury

But perhaps the bigger issue for the Wuhan Open tournament directors is that the top players who did compete failed to meet expectations. Only two seeded players remain in the draw: Iga Swiatek and Maja Chwalinska.

Aryna Sabalenka and Jessica Pegula, the top two seeds, both lost their opening matches, and the likes of Karolina Muchova, Belinda Bencic, Marta Kostyuk, and the Filipina sensation Alex Eala all failed to reach the quarter-finals.

That has left the Wuhan Open draw looking rather weak heading into finals weekend. The players competing for the title won't mind, though, with a WTA 1000 title on the line.

Why did so many players skip this year's Wuhan Open?

The simple answer is that the Wuhan Open has a nasty spot on the WTA calendar. It's right after the China Open in Beijing, and at a point in the year when many players are carrying knocks and winding down before the off-season.

If you know you are unable to qualify for the WTA Finals, why risk an injury in Wuhan? It makes more sense to rest up for a week and return at one of the upcoming WTA 500 events in Ningbo, China, or Tokyo, Japan.

There is no real solution for those in charge of the Wuhan Open, though, other than offering players bigger appearance fees. Whether the Wuhan Open can survive if another wave of withdrawals hits the event in 2027 remains to be seen.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka admits pressure has been difficult to handle as another Wuhan Open loss raises questions about her form
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka, the 28 year old Belarusian star athlete, has been going through a challenging time as she suffered a surprise Round of 32 loss to Ann Li
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka, the 28 year old Belarusian star athlete, has been going through a challenging time as she suffered a surprise Round of 32 loss to Ann Li at the Wuhan Open on October 14, 2026. The popular tennis star’s loss at the Wuhan Open comes just days after the loss at the China Open and the US Open. It seems she is going through a tough time and in an interview, Aryna Sabalenka had opened up about her mental health.Aryna Sabalenka reflects on her mental health as she goes through a tough timeA few days ago, in an interview, the 28 year old tennis star said, “I just think it's a combination of everything…You overthink, then you make easy mistakes, then you miss opportunities. “Then the other player on the other side steps in and starts playing a bit more aggressively and more free – kind of fearless.”The 4 Grand Slam single titles champion added, “Sometimes it's really tough to hold the pressure and put it back on the opponent.”Aryna Sabalenka continued, “I just have to sit back and openly think about what's going on in my head in those tough moments, because I'm quite an experienced player…I have been through so many things, and I overcame so many things. I just have to figure out that little thing that is not working for me sometimes, and hopefully I can overcome it.”She added, “You know those rooms where you just go in and you smash everything…Probably I will spend a whole day tomorrow over there destroying stuff.Aryna Sabalenka experiences consecutive losses on courtIn her most recent match on October 14, Aryna Sabalenka suffered a dramatic collapse against unseeded American Ann Li, losing 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5).The tennis star was up a set and a break (4-2) in the second set and went on to save 9 match points in the third before ultimately losing. articles.title: Djokovic jugará el torneo de Basilea para sumar puntos que le acerquen a las ATP Finals de Turín
articles.standfirst: El serbio ha aceptado la invitación de un torneo que no jugaba desde hacía 15 años
articles.summary: El serbio ha aceptado la invitación de un torneo que no jugaba desde hacía 15 años
articles.body: Novak Djokovic, después de renunciar los dos últimos años a participar en las ATP Finals de Turín, está dispuesto a luchar por una plaza para terminar la temporada entre los ocho mejores del curso. El serbio, que al igual como Carlos Alcaraz tenía en su agenda la semana que viene el Six Kings Slam de Riad, ha añadido a su calendario el Open 500 de Basilea. Al no estar apuntado al certamen, ha tenido que recibir una invitación de la organización. Su objetivo es conseguir puntos que le acerquen a una cita de maestros en la que ha sido campeón un total de siete ocasiones, una cifra récord. A sus 39 años, sabe que está ante la que puede ser la última oportunidad de volver a ganar el cetro. Nole no jugaba en Basilea desde la edición de 2011 en la que alcanzó las semifinales. La presencia de Rafa Jódar en las semifinales del Masters 1000 de Shanghái ha hecho que el serbio haya sido superado por el madrileño en la Race 2026. Ahora mismo es undécimo de la temporada, a 69 puntos del español, que cerraría hoy el cartel de titulares en Turín. El morbo está servido porque Jódar también participará en Basilea. Djokovic, que perdió en el debut de Shanghái con Hubert Hurkacz, venía de ganar su título 102 en Pekín. En Basilea puede igualar los 103 de Roger Federer, la leyenda suiza que precisamente nació en esa ciudad.

images.caption: Djokovic, en un entreno.

articles.title: Alcaraz aspira en Viena al bonus millonario de los torneos 500
articles.standfirst: El murciano es cuarto entre los tenistas con más puntos en eventos de la categoría
articles.summary: El murciano es cuarto entre los tenistas con más puntos en eventos de la categoría
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz aspira, por segundo año seguido, a llevarse el mayor botín de los torneos 500, que es el bonus a tenista que obtiene más puntos en los eventos de la categoría. Alcaraz, campeón en Doha y Tokio, es ahora mismo cuarto en la clasificación de 2026, con un total de 1.050 puntos. Por delante de él están Alex de Miñaur (1.280), Ben Shelton (1.250) y Taylor Fritz (1.160). Carlitos jugará del 26 de octubre al 1 de noviembre el Open 500 de Viena para intentar escalar posiciones y acabar como líder en puntuación. Esa misma semana se juega Basilea, que reparte los mismos puntos. De Miñaur, al igual que el murciano, está apuntado en la capital austriaca mientras que Shelton y Fritz aparecen en la lista de inscritos de la localidad helvética. La bolsa en premios que destina la ATP para los 16 mejores en los torneos 500 es de 3.070.000 dólares. El que acabe primero se llevará aproximadamente un millón de dólares, 512.500 el segundo, y 256.250 el tercero. El fenómeno de El Palmar verá como se le aplica una reducción del 15 por ciento sobre el total porque no pudo participar en Queen's debido a la lesión en su muñeca. Hay tres giras de eventos obligatorios durante el curso. La primera engloba Rotterdam, Río, Doha, Dallas, Dubái, Acapulco, Barcelona y Múnich. La segunda contempla Hamburgo, Queen's, Halle y Washington y la tercera Pekín, Tokio, Viena y Basilea.

articles.summary: El mallorquín es el único español presente en el cuadro del torneo de categoría 250
articles.body: El tenis masculino español tendrá un único representante en el cuadro del Open 250 de Bruselas. Se trata de Jaume Munar. El mallorquín, el 49 del mundo, debutará contra un rival procedente de la fase previa. En caso de pasar la criba inicial le esperaría Arthur Fils, primer favorito del certamen y que busca puntos que le acerquen a las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). El francés es ahora mismo octavo de la Race 2026, con 3.380 puntos. Pero Rafa Jódar le echa el aliento gracias a su semifinal en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái y podría pasarle en caso de levantar el título del TMS chino.

articles.title: Badosa se estrena sin técnico en Osaka contra la croata Ruzic
articles.standfirst: La catalana rompió su relación profesional con Pol Toledo a la conclusión del WTA 1000 de Pekín
articles.summary: La catalana rompió su relación profesional con Pol Toledo a la conclusión del WTA 1000 de Pekín
articles.body: Paula Badosa regresa a la competición oficial la semana que viene en el WTA 250 de Osaka. Lo hará por primera vez en cuatro años sin la presencia de Pol Toledo en su banquillo. La tenista rompió la relación con su entrenador a la conclusión del reciente WTA 1000 de Pekín. Así lo reconoció ella misma el viernes a través de sus redes sociales. En la capital china se había despedido en la segunda ronda tras ceder ante la letona Jelena Ostapenko. Badosa, acompañada por el 'sparring' Carlos Silvestre, se estrenará en tierras japonesas contra la croata Antonia Ruzic, la 93 del ranking y a la que ya derrotó en el único precedente entre ambas. Paula, la 58 de las listas y que el próximo 15 de noviembre cumple 29 años, busca puntos que le permitan mejorar su clasificación. Terminará la temporada jugando en Guangzhou (26 de octubre al 1 de noviembre) y Hong Kong (2 al 8 de noviembre). La tenista de Begur no será la única española presente en el cuadro de Osaka. Allí también reaparece Kaitlin Quevedo, que estrenó su palmarés de títulos en septiembre en el WTA de Sao Paulo. Quevedo se las verá de inicio con la tailandesa Lanlana Tararudee.

articles.title: Davidovich hace magia ante Zverev y se planta en la final de Shanghái
articles.standfirst: El malagueño remonta un set al virtual número 1 y buscará el tercer título de la temporada
articles.summary: El malagueño remonta un set al virtual número 1 y buscará el tercer título de la temporada
articles.body: La primera de las dos balas del tenis masculino español para tener un representante en la final de Shanghái ha resultado exitosa. Alejandro Davidovich se ha clasificado este sábado para la última ronda del torneo tras remontar a Alexander Zverev y cerrar un tanteo favorable de 5-7, 6-4 y 6-3, en 2 horas y 2 minutos. Davidovich se mete en su octava final, la tercera de la presente campaña. Cabe recordar que en 2026, estrenó su palmarés en el Mallorca Championships y le siguió Chengdu. El Masters 1000 de Shanghái, que es el único que se le resiste a la Armada', puede caer en su decimoquinta edición. Lo aseguraría una victoria a continuación de Rafa Jódar ante Daniil Medvedev. De momento, Álex es el cuarto español que luchará por la corona el último domingo tras Rafael Nadal (2009, 2017), David Ferrer (2011) y Roberto Bautista (2016). A pesar de haberse perdido toda la gira americana de pista dura por sus problemas de espalda, y quedarse sin entrenador en mitad de Roland Garros, el tenista de Fuengirola escala a la decimocuarta posición del ranking, la mejor de su carrera. La fuerza mental de Álex se demostró con la pelota de eliminación que levantó en la tercera ronda con Frances Tiafoe. "Defensa siciliana, vamos", firmó en la cámara de la realización. "Sabía que iba a tener mis opciones y la rotura en el tercer set me ha dado más energía", decía a la conclusión. Zverev, con una movilidad reducida por sus molestias en el tobillo al apoyar con el pie derecho, supo leer mejor el partido al inicio y esperó su momento. Este llegó en el undécimo juego cuando se hizo con el saque de su rival. El alemán juega con la confianza de saberse número 1. Lo será seguro el próximo 2 de noviembre si gana el Open 500 de Viena donde coincidirá en el cuadro con Carlos Alcaraz. Sascha se mostró inmenso al saque, ayudado por la rapidez extrema de la central del Qi Zhong. La mitad de sus servicios no volvían. Ni su excelencia en este apartado le permitió pasar a su decimocuarta final de un torneo TMS. Davidovich decantó a su favor los mejores puntos del partido en los que se pudo comprobar el buen rollo entre los dos protagonistas. Ambos se ven mucho las caras porque residen en Montecarlo. Sascha fue a lo práctico, esperando más los errores no forzados que llegaban desde el otro lado de la red. El alemán se había impuesto en seis de los siete precedentes. El pupilo de Pepo Clavet tuvo dos puntos de break en el cuarto juego del segundo parcial. Era su primer aviso porque en el siguiente se llevó el segundo set con un magistral pasante de revés. A Zverev le pesaron la cantidad de partidos acumulados a sus espaldas ante un verdugo con más chispa y más ganas de tocar la gloria. Nadie ha ganado más que el de Hamburgo en esta temporada (62 victorias), de las que 33 son en superficie dura. Esos números se fueron al limbo ante el talentoso jugador andaluz. Pudo cerrar al resto, con 5-2 y 15-40. Lo hizo inmediatamente después al saque. Lo celebró a medias porque falta lo más importante. Rafa Jódar saltará a continuación frente a Daniil Medvedev para hacer doblete de españoles en la final y garantizar el título.

images.caption: La firma de Álex en la cámara.
Zverev, durante el partido. ALEX PLAVEVSKI
Álex ejecuta una dejada.

articles.title: Rafa Jódar - Daniil Medvedev en directo | Semifinales del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, en vivo
articles.summary: Rafa Jódar - Daniil Medvedev 6-3, 1-0. Saca Jódar. No sabe por donde salir el ruso. Totalemnete bloqueado por el juego del español. Confirma el break
articles.body:
Buenas tardes, bienvenidos a las semifinales del Masters 1000 de Shanghái. El torneo de mayor importancia en esta gira asiática. Hoy tendremos en la pista central del Centro de Tenis Qizhong a Rafa Jódar, que se las verá ante el ruso Daniil Medvedev, por un hueco en la final del certamen asiático. El partido se disputará alrededor de las 19:00 horas (horario local).

El tenista madrileño lleva acumuladas 9 horas y 34 minutos en pista, pero está acostumbrado a ello. Es la quinta semifinal de la temporada y le permite soñar con dos marcas: el récord de Boris Becker de ser el más rápido en pasar del top100 al top10 y dar un paso más en sus aspiraciones de estar en las Nitto ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). Está a tan solo 341 puntos de las primeras diez posiciones.

Se medirá al campeón de Grand Slam, Daniil Medvedev. No existen precedentes entre ambos. El ruso llega en su mejor nivel de la temporada, con 11 de 12 victorias en sus últimos encuentros de la presente gira asiática. Será todo un reto para Rafa Jódar.

articles.title: Emma Raducanu: Retired Brit Dan Evans predicts former US Open champion 'will win Wimbledon' despite injuries and fitness issues
articles.summary: Emma Raducanu has dropped out of the world’s top 100 after missing Wimbledon and the US Open due to injury; You can watch the WTA Wuhan Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports.
articles.body:
The 23-year-old suffered a stress fracture in her lower right leg and was forced to miss both Wimbledon and the US Open .

Raducanu has dropped to world No 107, her lowest position in two years, but Evans, who retired at this year's Wimbledon after controversially being denied a singles wildcard, has backed her to win the grass-court title on home soil.

"I genuinely think she will win Wimbledon one day," Evans told The Telegraph.

"Yeah, I don't know why. She's good, and I think - I'm saying this in as nice a way as possible - I think she thinks she's good.

"Not in an arrogant way, but when she plays big matches, she's like 'Whatever. This is just another match.' And yeah, I just think one day she'll get it."

It has been a frustrating 12 months for Raducanu with more persistent physical issues. After a foot injury severely hampered her pre-season training, Raducanu then spent two-and-a-half months off court with a post-viral illness after initially falling unwell in early February.

She finally returned for the end of the clay-court season having rehired Andrew Richardson, the coach who guided her to the US Open title, but the pair's time on court together has been limited.

Raducanu was not among the players named in Great Britain's team for the Billie Jean King Cup Finals in late September and with question marks over whether she will compete again in 2026.

The former world No 10 could benefit from ending her season early to focus on recovery and secure a protected ranking before making her return next year.

"There's no doubt she needs to have a racket in her hand a bit more," said Evans. "I'm sure she's getting pushed side-to-side by endorsements, and there's a bit of tug of war on what she needs to do, what she doesn't.

"I admit I've not watched her practices very often, but from what I'm told she's a good trainer: she works for two, three hours in a row with hardly any break."

Should Raducanu miss at least six months of competition due to injury, she can use a special ranking for a select number of events upon her return.

This would be her top-50 ranking from during the grass season - the last time she competed and received prize money for a tournament.

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis , former player-turned-TV analyst Annabel Croft said:

"It wouldn't be a surprise if she made that decision [close down her season]. That wouldn't be such a bad decision to take because you can fully heal, rest up, get as much treatment as possible and then come out fully fit, raring to go at the start of next year.

"Maybe if there's a worry about the ranking drop with so many points to defend and potentially that ranking could plummet, although she might benefit from the protected ranking.

"All of these factors have to be considered, don't they? But at the end of the day, your health is your wealth, as they say, and that is the most important factor and she just needs to get herself fit.

"It's an unusual injury. I mean, I've had calf muscle injuries, which were not nice at all. And the minute you push off, you tweak it and it feels tight but the one thing that I've always thought about Raducanu, particularly when we saw her at Queen's Club on the grass where she played such beautiful tennis, is that she's very light on her feet. Movement has always been one of her strengths.

"She's such a great athlete. She moves around the ball. She's light on her feet and gets into great positions where she never looks off balance. But movement will be part of a major strength of what she brings out onto the court. That needs to be absolutely 100 per cent."

articles.title: Wuhan Open: Sonay Kartal beats Jelena Ostapenko to reach first WTA 1,000 final of her career
articles.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal beats former French Open winner Jelena Ostapenko to reach the Wuhan Open final in only her third event after a six-month injury lay-off.
articles.body:
Sonay Kartal's dream week continued as she beat former Grand Slam champion Jelena Ostapenko at the Wuhan Open to reach the biggest final of her career.

British number five Kartal is playing in only her third event since returning from a six-month absence with a back injury, but she now stands one more victory away from a WTA 1,000 title - one of the most prestigious prizes outside of the Grand Slams.

The 24-year-old's composure helped her secure a 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory in a pulsating semi-final against Latvia's Ostapenko.

Kartal trailed 4-1 in both sets but remained level-headed and took advantage when 34th-ranked Ostapenko stuttered in high-pressure moments.

Remarkably, Kartal survived three set points in the first set, and three more set points in the second, to secure a victory which will long live in the memory.

"That was probably one of the toughest matches I've ever played," said Kartal.

"At times she is unplayable and you have to ride that wave. Mentally, this is one of the best performances of my career."

The world number 170 is the lowest-ranked player to reach a WTA 1,000 final since the format was introduced in 1990.

Kartal, who was ranked 54th immediately before her long lay-off, will play either six-time Grand Slam winner Iga Swiatek or French Open finalist Maja Chwalinska in Sunday's final.

Reaching the final means Kartal, who has been as high as 44th in the world, will return to the world's top 50 and become Britain's number one player when the next rankings are released on Monday.

Kartal enjoys 'best week of career' after diving into deep end

A difficult season for Kartal is ending on a euphoric high which even she did not see coming.

Coming back after such a long absence can often require time and patience as a player's game slowly returns, but Kartal has been able to produce a level which even she is pleasantly surprised to be reaching so soon.

After making her comeback when playing for Great Britain at the BJK Cup little over three weeks ago, Kartal earned a couple of confidence-boosting wins at the Beijing Open and has carried that momentum into Wuhan.

With consistent hitting from the baseline, supreme athleticism and tenacity, Kartal moved into the last four with notable wins over Tokyo Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, 2024 Wimbledon runner-up Jasmine Paolini and four-time major semi-finalist Elina Svitolina.

Ostapenko, a heavy hitter who can hammer countless winners but also be extremely erratic, presented Kartal with a very different challenge to those opponents.

At the start of the biggest match of her career, it looked ominous for Kartal.

Ostapenko stepped in to hammer away a pair of backhand winners off second serves in the first two points of the match, applying early pressure which led to an immediate break of Kartal's serve.

The early advantage allowed former world number five Ostapenko to play freely - serving big and striking ferociously - leaving Kartal unable to impose her game as she trailed by a double break at 4-1.

But Ostapenko's tendency to self-combust allowed Kartal to turn around a set which became increasingly dramatic.

Kartal clawed one of the breaks back as Ostapenko, the 2017 French Open winner, became wayward from the baseline, before the Latvian steadied herself - pummelling more aces and winners - to move a hold away from the opening set.

However, Ostapenko became agitated as she twice failed to serve out the opening set at 5-4 and 6-5 - and Kartal took advantage in a pulsating tie-break.

An equally dramatic second set followed a similar pattern, ending in the same outcome.

Kartal had to survive a barrage from the other side of the net at times - Ostapenko finishing with 50 winners and nine aces - but the Briton's ability to keep her emotions on a more even keel again proved crucial.

articles.title: Medvedev amenaza al juez de silla durante la semifinal: "Si no me enseñas la bola me voy de la pista"
articles.standfirst: El ruso quiso ver una pelota de Jódar que había botado claramente sobre la línea
articles.summary: El ruso quiso ver una pelota de Jódar que había botado claramente sobre la línea
articles.body: Daniil Medvedev no ha cambiado. Quien piense que la descalificación de Pekín le va a hacer modificar su manera de ser en la pista se equivoca. Una muestra de ello el nuevo incidente que ha protagonizado este sábado durante la semifinal del Masters 1000 de Shanghái que le enfrentaba a Rafa Jódar. En el sexto juego del partido, tras una pelota dudosa, el ruso se dirigió al árbitro para pedir que le enseñaran la repetición. El juez de silla le indicó que la regla sólo permite ver el último bote de la jugada. Fue entonces cuando Medvedev amenazo con irse: "Si no me enseñas la bola me voy". El árbitro, para evitar otro show del moscovita, llamó por teléfono al VAR del tenis para que mostraran la imagen de la pelota de Jódar botando claramente sobre la línea. Ver para creer que se cambie el protocolo porque a Daniil le apetezca.

articles.body: Rafa Jódar, después de anotarse la manga inicial de la segunda semifinal del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, ha pedido rápidamente la presencia del fisioterapeuta del torneo. articles.title: Sonay Kartal: British star digs deep to beat Jelena Ostapenko and secure a spot in her first-ever WTA 1000 final
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal defeats Jelena Ostapenko to reach her first-ever WTA 1000 final against former world No 1 Iga Swiatek or French Open finalist Maja Chwalinska; You can watch the WTA Wuhan Open final - live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 11.30am
articles.body:
Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Ostapenko.

Currently 170th in the WTA rankings, Kartal will break inside the top 50 and become the new British No 1 after becoming the lowest-ranked player to reach the final in Wuhan.

The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match.

Kartal, who made her breakthrough by reaching the fourth round of last year's Wimbledon, said: "That was one of the toughest matches I've played.

"I know exactly how she was going to play. At times she's unplayable, but sometimes you have to ride that wave and mentally this is one of the best performances I've had in my career so very proud of that one.

"I was dreaming of playing this match before the injury so to be able to come back here in my third event and to achieve this regardless is a huge milestone for me, so I'm going to recover and enjoy every second tomorrow."

After reaching the fourth round of Indian Wells in March, Kartal missed six months with a stress fracture in her back, returning last month at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals.

Kartal, previously ranked as high as No 44 in the world, reached the third round in Beijing last week.

In Wuhan, she has swept past world No 48 Anhelina Kalinina, world No 12 Belinda Bencic, two-time Grand Slam singles finalist Jasmine Paolini, four-time major semi-finalist Svitolina, and now former French Open champion Ostapenko.

Kartal missed three of this year's four Grand Slams, including Wimbledon.

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis , Colin Fleming said: "Her ability to stay in the present got her through. She kept cool to ultimately outlast Ostapenko, who hit 50 winners past her and still couldn't win a set.

"Just a brilliant achievement and the run doesn't stop here. She's playing the tennis of her life and she's got every chance of getting her hands on the title."

articles.title: Jódar acaba con Medvedev y se cita con Davidovich en la fiesta nacional de Shanghái
articles.standfirst: El tenis español inscribirá su nombre en el único Masters 1000 que se le resistía
articles.summary: El tenis español inscribirá su nombre en el único Masters 1000 que se le resistía
articles.body: El duelo fratricida entre Rafa Jódar y Alejandro Davidovich garantiza el título español en el torneo de Shanghái. El único Masters 1000 que se le resistía a la 'Armada' también ha claudicado a la excelencia de las raquetas nacionales. Después de la victoria de Álex ante Alexander Zverev le secundó el joven Rafa, tras acabar con la resistencia de Daniil Medvedev, por 6-3 y 6-4, en 1 hora y 44 minutos. Al ruso no le sirvió la experiencia, no en vano se había coronado en el certamen en 2019, y tampoco sus artimañas. Llegó a amenazar al árbitro con retirarse si no le mostraban una bola que él consideraba mala y fue botó claramente sobre la línea. Ya son nueve las finales netamente españolas en eventos TMS desde su introducción en 1990. La primera fue en 1996, con Roberto Carretero y Álex Corretja. La última, en 2017, con Rafael Nadal y Albert Ramos. Nueve años después, España vuelve a ejercer de gran potencia del tenis. Porque tiene calidad y cantidad. Lo sabe David Ferrer, que tendrá un arsenal infinito a sus órdenes para conquistar la séptima Ensaladera de la historia. Las alarmas sonaron cuando Jódar pidió marcharse a los vestuarios para ser atendido por el fisioterapeuta. Sufría por el esfuerzo y la humedad. Son 73 partidos a sus espaldas, de los que 56 ha decantado a su favor. Medvedev, totalmente contrariado, salvó las tres primeras bolas de final en el noveno juego al saque. No podría neutralizar más desde el resto. En Shanghái todo es español: desde la comida del restaurante Cambio de Tercio a los dos finalistas. La vigésima victoria de Rafa en Masters 1000 le sitúa como el segundo más joven en alcanzar esa cifra, sólo por detrás de Nadal. Es el más precoz luchando por todo en el mejor torneo de China. El de Leganés disputará su tercera final tras Marrakech y Washington. El madrileño tendrá un doble botín en juego este domingo en Shanghái. Y es que el trofeo vale también la condición de 'top10'. Está ahora a 91 puntos de Arthur Fils. Le permitiría, además, batir el récord de Boris Becker, como el más rápido en pasar del 'top100' a las diez primeras posiciones. Los 3.159 puntos sumados en el presente curso le afianzan como el número nueve de la Race 2026 y le sitúan un poco más cerca de las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). Le saca 279 puntos a Alex de Miñaur y 319 a Novak Djokovic.

articles.summary: No hay precedentes entre los dos jugadores españoles
articles.body: El tenis masculino español vivirá una fiesta este domingo en Shanghái. Rafa Jódar y Alejandro Davidovich se jugarán la corona del penúltimo Masters 1000 del curso, el único evento de la categoría que aún no figuraba en el palmarés de la Armada. Será el primer enfrentamiento entre el joven madrileño, que bate récords de precocidad, y su compatriota malagueño. Davidovich se ha ganado el derecho a su segunda final de un TMS tras deshacerse de Alexander Zverev. Por su parte, Jódar se estrenará después de haber eliminado al campeón de Shanghái 2019. Para Álex puede ser la tercera corona del curso, tras el Mallorca Championships y Chengdu. En el caso de Rafa sería la segunda después de imponerse en abril sobre la tierra batida de Marrakech. La gran final del Masters 1000 de Shanghái se celebrará este domingo 18 de octubre en la central del Qi Zhong, a partir de las 10:30 horas en España. El partido decisivo del torneo de Shanghái se podrá ver en directo a través de Movistar Plus. La mejor información estará en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev 'overachieved' with Shanghai semi-final run
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev says he "overachieved" at the Shanghai Masters in reaching the semi-finals amid fatigue caused by his busy schedule.
articles.body:
World number two Alexander Zverev said he "overachieved" at the Shanghai Masters in reaching the semi-finals amid fatigue caused by his busy competition schedule.

The 29-year-old top seed exited in the last four on Saturday as Spaniard Alejandro Davidovich Fokina pulled off a surprise 5-7 6-4 6-3 win, only his second in eight meetings with Zverev.

Germany's Zverev, who is guaranteed to end the season as world number one, has had little opportunity to rest between the US Open, Laver Cup, Beijing Masters and Shanghai.

"I feel like I've actually, in a way, maybe overachieved this week because of how much tennis I played," Zverev said.

"I carried a little bit of injury, I carried fatigue into the tournament, and I'm OK to lose to a player like this today."

Kartal reaches Wuhan final as dream week continues

Serb player banned to 2050 for tennis match-fixing

Repeatedly exposed on the forehand side, Zverev surrendered his first break of the match to an exquisite backhand passing shot on the run as Davidovich Fokina took the semi-final to a deciding set.

Zverev was broken to trail 2-0 in the third set and could not recover control of the tie as the 25th seed advanced to his first ATP Masters 1000 final since 2022.

Having failed to replicate the performance which earned him a straight-set win over Alex de Minaur in the quarter-final, Zverev said he has struggled since his fourth-round win over Alexander Bublik went to a third-set tie-break.

"First, I'm not a robot, I'm a human being, I get tired," Zverev said. "After the US Open, I had one day off in total. I think I played a lot of tennis, which is very, very positive because that means I played well.

"I think even here I had tough matches. I personally feel like I was quite flat since the Bublik match, because I was losing energy.

"I played a phenomenal match against Alex de Minaur, but today I was flat. Even in the first set, even though I won the set, I was flatter, I was not reacting so well. I was returning quite badly.

"We're all human beings, even the best players in the world."

His semi-final defeat is a disappointing exception to a brilliant season for Zverev, who claimed the first Grand Slam title of his career at the French Open in June before winning a second at the US Open in September.

Davidovich Fokina will face fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar in the final on Sunday.

articles.title: Roger Federer And On Target Tennis Growth In China
articles.summary: Roger Federer and On host On Thanks for Playing event as part the effort to grow tennis in China. The event included floating tennis court and drone show.
articles.body:
Earlier this week, Roger Federer played on a floating tennis court while 2,000 drones formed animated images of him hitting his iconic one-handed backhand over the skies of Shenzhen, China.

Two days later, Federer teamed with International Tennis Hall of Famers Li Na and Marat Safin in a celebrity exhibition at the Shanghai Masters.

Whether floating on water, soaring in the heavens, or teaming up with stars, Federer aims to grow tennis in China.

The floating court was installed at Shenzhen Talent Park for "On Thanks for Playing," a celebration of the sport. Federer is an On co-entrepreneur and involved in product development.

Roger Federer's Connection To Growing Tennis In China

The Thanks for Playing event reunited Federer with the Wild Elephant Tennis Club, a grassroots training program primarily for children in Yunnan Province's mountainous regions in Southwest China. This is the third year Federer has connected with the Wild Elephant kids.

After the first meeting, On incorporated motifs from an original hand-painted drawing by one of the kids into the shoe's graphic detailing and custom sockliner.

"It's always something I really enjoy, and I hope these experiences inspire the kids to keep playing, learning, and most importantly, having fun with the sport," Federer told Forbes.com in an email interview. "Every time I meet young players, I'm reminded of the excitement and passion that comes with discovering tennis."

"It's not just about sharing my experiences with these kids," Federer said. "I take just as much inspiration from them, and it reminds me why I fell in love with tennis in the first place and why I'm so passionate about what we're building together with On."

Federer's commitment to growing the game in China is ongoing, and he holds the record for the most titles at the Shanghai Masters. Novak Djokovic sought to tie Federer's record for most titles at the event, but fell short after losing in the first round.

Despite his retirement, Federer remains present at ATP Tour events, promoting philanthropic and entrepreneurial pursuits . He's one of the wealthiest tennis players in the history of the sport.

Growth in China has been a bright spot for On, which opened its largest flagship store in China, in Shenzhen, in March.

"On's net sales in the Asia-Pacific region grew 96.4% year-over-year in 2025. China, now the second-largest market globally and one of the fastest-growing, has become a key focus for future development. We will maintain our DTC strategy to engage with consumers directly," said Britt Olsen, Chief Commercial Officer at On, in a press release in March. "Following footwear, apparel has emerged as the second major growth engine. In China, the category shows tremendous potential. We will continue to expand our retail footprint and further enhance the brand experience."

However, On suffered a setback after reporting missed sales expectations in August . The Business of Fashion reported that "constant-currency net sales grew 13 percent in the Americas in the second quarter, slower than the 55 percent growth in Asia-Pacific and 21 percent in Europe, the Middle East and Africa," and that dynamic is one reason On kept its sneakers and apparel prices steady at a time when many brands resorted to markdowns.

"It's been wonderful to see the passion and enthusiasm for tennis in China, especially among the younger generation," Federer said. "Through On Thanks for Playing, we have a great opportunity to connect with these young players and encourage them to continue enjoying the sport. . . Hopefully, through initiatives like these and the work we're doing with On, we can play a small part in inspiring more young people in China to pick up a racket and stay involved in tennis."

During the On Thanks for Playing event, Federer shared the floating court with standout junior players Fa Wang, Xinya Xiao, Siyan Jiang and Zixi Yang.

"There is a genuine, joyful energy across China's tennis community right now that touches all of us," said Rebecca Cai, Chief Global Markets Officer at On, in a press release . "To see Roger back here, reconnecting with the community and sharing a rally on the water with the next generation of players is pure magic."
